SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl came upon the Prophet praying and forbade him, prompting the passage about the one who forbids a servant when he prays through the sinful, lying forelock.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاءه أبو جهل فنهاه فأنزل الله ﴿ أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ﴾

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r8.claim: Here raʾayta is inward seeing used to mean tell me; its first object is the forbidding man, and the first hypothetical asks whether the servant is guided in worshipping God or commanded to piety.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r8.anchor: {أرءيت} رؤية قلبية معناه أخبرني ذلك الناهي وهو المفعول الأول {إن كان على الهدى} فيما ينهى عنه من عبادة الله {أو أمر بالتقوى}

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r9.claim: The first conditional’s omitted answer is supplied by the next conditional’s answer, since an interrogative or oath clause must complete the object of raʾayta.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r9.anchor: وهذه الجملة الشرطية بجوابها المحذوف وهو ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى سدت مسد المفعول الثاني

QASHANI:96:9-14/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:9-14/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:9-14/r2.claim: The hypothetical question about whether the worshipper is guided or commands piety voices the arrogant denier’s own misguided claim and invitation to associationism.
QASHANI:96:9-14/r2.anchor: في شركه ودعوته إلى الشرك فرضا وتقديرا كما زعم

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r12.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether it would not be better if the worshipper were guided or commanded piety.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r12.anchor: أرأيت إن كان على الهدى أو أمر بالتقوى } . لكان خيرا له

IBNASHUR:96:12/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:12/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:12/r1.claim: Another hypothetical intensifies the wonder: would the opponent forbid a servant firmly guided, or one who commands piety? Since he forbids prayer, he forbids guidance and may also forbid counsel to piety.
IBNASHUR:96:12/r1.anchor: أو إن كان العبد آمراً بالتقوى أينهاه عن ذلك

IBNASHUR:96:12/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:12/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:12/r2.claim: The conditional answer is omitted and inferred as “would he forbid him too”; in answers, in leaves the condition's occurrence uncertain to match the scenario.
IBNASHUR:96:12/r2.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف وأتى بحرف الشرط الذي الغالب فيه عدم الجزم بوقوع فعل الشرط

IBNASHUR:96:12/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:12/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:12/r3.claim: Raʾayta is cognitive, with its two objects omitted; ʿalā expresses figurative elevation, the servant's firm establishment in guidance, as in Luqmān.
IBNASHUR:96:12/r3.anchor: للاستعلاء المجازي وهو شدّة التمكن من الهُدى

IBNASHUR:96:12/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:12/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:12/r4.claim: The hidden subjects of kāna and amara refer to the servant, even though nearby pronouns refer to the forbidding person; context resolves each pronoun's antecedent.
IBNASHUR:96:12/r4.anchor: عائدان إلى { عبداً } وإن كانت الضمائر الحافّة به عائدة إلى

IBNASHUR:96:12/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:12/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:12/r5.claim: ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās's verse illustrates that pronouns can refer to different antecedents according to context.
IBNASHUR:96:12/r5.anchor: قول عباس بن مرداس : عُدنا ولولا نَحْنُ

IBNASHUR:96:12/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:12/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:12/r6.claim: The object of raʾayta is understood from the prior “forbids” or from the following reminder that God sees; the repeated hypothetical is separated because it renews the wonder about one person.
IBNASHUR:96:12/r6.anchor: لوقوعها موقع التكرير لأن فيها تكرير التَّعجيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r7.claim: A second hypothetical astonishment asks whether the forbidding man would also obstruct a servant who is rightly guided or commands piety.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p446/r7.anchor: أتظنه ينهى أيضا عبدا متمكنا من الهدى فتعجب من نهيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r1.claim: Stopping prayer means stopping a devotional act, and thus stopping guidance; Abu Jahl might even forbid someone from commanding piety.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r1.anchor: من ينهى عن الصلاة وهي قربة إلى الله فقد نهى عن الهدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r2.claim: The conditional particle, usually used when the condition is uncertain, matches the stance of the man who forbids the servant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r2.anchor: وأتى بحرف الشرط الذي الغالب فيه عدم الجزم بوقوع فعل الشرط مجاراة لحال الذي ينهى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r5.claim: In the conditionals, the hidden pronouns refer back to the servant, despite nearby pronouns referring to the forbidding man; context restores each pronoun to its proper antecedent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r5.anchor: فإن السياق يرد كل ضمير إلى معاده كما في قول عباس بن مرداس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r6.claim: The second object of “have you seen” is omitted and can be understood from verse 14 or from the earlier “forbids”; the implied question is whether he would forbid him too.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r6.anchor: إن كان على الهدى أو أمر بالتقوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r7.claim: The clause is detached because it repeats the astonishment about several possible states of the same person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r7.anchor: لوقوعها موقع التكرير لأن فيها تكرير التعجيب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.claim: God asks whether the forbidding opponent realizes that God sees and hears him, and will repay him fully for what he does.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.anchor: أي: أما علم هذا الناهي لهذا المهتدي أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء.

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r11.claim: If the worshiper is rightly guided and the tyrant forbidding prayer and piety is mistaken, the latter destroys himself; the command to piety may specifically describe the Prophet or every worshiper who calls to right.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r11.anchor: لو أن هذا المصلي كان على هدى وطريق الحق فعلا واعتقادا، وأن هذا الطاغي المانع من الصلاة،

KASHSHAF:96:12/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:12/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:12/r1.claim: Or suppose he commands what he believes is good and piety, namely worship of idols.
KASHSHAF:96:12/r1.anchor: أو كان آمراً بالمعروف والتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقد

MUQATIL:96:9-19/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r2.claim: The guided person in the question is Muhammad, and being commanded to piety means being commanded to sincerity.
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r2.anchor: يعني محمدا { على الهدى } [آية: 11] { أو أمر بالتقوى }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#6/r1.claim: The alternative asks whether he commands righteousness and piety in what he advocates—worship of idols, as he supposes.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#6/r1.anchor: أو كان آمرا بالمعروف والتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقد

QURTUBI-FULL:96:11-12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:11-12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:11-12/r1.claim: The rhetorical question asks Abu Jahl whether he realizes that opposing Muhammad, if he is rightly guided and commands piety and prayer, will bring ruin on the opponent.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:11-12/r1.anchor: أي أرأيت يا أبا جهل إن كان محمد على هذه الصفة، أليس ناهيه عن التقوى والصلاة هالكا؟!

QUTB-ZILAL:96:12/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:12/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:12/r1.claim: The prohibition is especially outrageous if the worshiper himself is guided and urges others toward piety.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:12/r1.anchor: مع أنه على الهدى ،  آمر بالتقوى

RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r1.claim: The first view makes both araʾayta passages address the Prophet; their matching addressee preserves the discourse's rhetorical order, and asks whether the unbeliever might instead follow guidance and care for himself.
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r1.anchor: أنه خطاب للنبي عليه السلام ، والدليل عليه أن الأول وهو قوله

RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r2.claim: On that reading, a rational, prosperous man would do better to choose faith, guidance, and enjoining piety than disbelief and forbidding worship; the passage laments his lost higher station.
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r2.anchor: أما كان ذلك خيرا له من الكفر بالله والنهي عن خدمته وطاعته

RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r3.claim: The second view addresses the unbeliever: God, like a judge or master hearing opposing parties, turns from the Prophet to ask whether he would forbid a man whose prayer guides and commands piety.

RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r4.claim: Prayer and calling others to God are the two things that troubled Abu Jahl, so both are named.
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r4.anchor: الذي شق على أبي جهل من أفعال الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام هو هذان الأمران

RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r5.claim: The Prophet was always either reforming himself through prayer or reforming others by commanding piety.
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r5.anchor: إما في إصلاح نفسه ، وذلك بفعل الصلاة أو في إصلاح غيره

RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r6.claim: The Prophet's prayer itself was guidance and an exhortation to piety: witnessing it softened hearts and inclined people to faith, making action a stronger call than speech.
RAZI-FULL:v32p21#3/r6.anchor: فكان فعل الصلاة دعوة بلسان الفعل ، وهو أقوى من الدعوة بلسان القول

TAB:96:14/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:14/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:14/r2.claim: The three repetitions of araʾayta work by substitution; the sense is whether the forbidding, denying man knows that God sees him.
TAB:96:14/r2.anchor: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ،   أرأيت إن كان على الهدى } ،   فكررت أرأيت مرات ثلاثا على البدل

TAB-FULL:v24p535/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p535/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p535/r2.claim: The second hypothetical asks whether Muhammad has commanded the one forbidding prayer to fear God and His punishment.
TAB-FULL:v24p535/r2.anchor: أو أمر محمد هذا الذي ينهى عن الصلاة، باتقاء الله، وخوف عقابه

TAB-FULL:v24p535/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p535/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p535/r3.claim: Qatada says Muhammad was on guidance and commanded piety.
TAB-FULL:v24p535/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {أرأيت إن كان على الهدى أو أمر بالتقوى} [العلق: 12] قال محمد: كان على الهدى، وأمر بالتقوى

ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n6/r1.claim: Taqwa is rendered throughout as God-consciousness; this is the earliest occurrence in revelation, and Asad interprets the opponent's invocation of religion as plainly not intended to deepen others' God-consciousness.
ASAD-NOTES:96:9#n6/r1.anchor: the obvious implication being that this is not his aim

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#2/r1.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#2/r1.claim: Taqwā means fearing God and refraining from His disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#2/r1.anchor: قال عطاء: مخافة الله، والتناهي عن معاصي الله (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#2/r2.claim: Muqātil interprets taqwā as sincerity and monotheism, meaning avoidance of associating partners with God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#2/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني بالإخلاص والتوحيد (¬3). ويكون المعنى على هذا باتقاء الشرك.

WAHIDI-QT:96:12/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:12/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:12/r1.claim: The repeated “have you seen?” is an expression of amazement, also used of the guided person who commands piety.
WAHIDI-QT:96:12/r1.anchor: ومعنى أرأيت ها هنا تعجب ،   وكذلك قوله { أرأيت إن كان على الهدى } { أو أمر بالتقوى }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r4.claim: The worshipper is on guidance and commands reverence for God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r4.anchor: أرأيت إن كان على الهدى }. { أو أمر بالتقوى }.

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r10.claim: The conditional sentence has an omitted consequence, and the pronouns in “was upon guidance” and “commanded piety” may refer either to the servant or to the prohibitor, shifting the addressee accordingly.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r10.anchor: bu kaziyye şartiyye olduğundan cezâsı mahzuftur. كَانَ، اَمَرَ zamirleri “abd”e de nehyedene de râci‘olabilir

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r11.claim: If the pronouns refer to the praying servant, the address turns to the tyrant: would it be bad if the servant followed truth or urged others to fear God and avoid evil?
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r11.anchor: “Düşünsene ey namaz kılan bir kulu nehyeden azgın insan! Eğer o kul hidâyet

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r12.claim: If the pronouns refer to the prohibitor, the address remains with the worshipper: how much better if the prohibitor followed guidance or urged piety instead of stopping prayer?
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r12.anchor: Nehyedene râci‘olduğu takdirde ise hitab, yine evvelki siyakta olarak “abd”e müteveccih olup

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.claim: Al-Kashshaf allows both conditional clauses to have expressed consequences, but the author prefers treating them as omitted and the following statement as an independent resumption.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.anchor: Keşşâf’ın dediği gibi iki şartın ikisinin de cevâbı yapmak câiz olsa bile şartların cezâları mahzuf olarak bunun bir cümle-i istînâfiye olması daha muvâfıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.claim: A universal reading is more suitable: all tyrants in every age who obstruct religion's work of shaping social life by goodness, truth, and justice are criticized.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.anchor: her dönemde görülen ve dinin sosyal hayatı iyilik, hak ve adalet ilkeleri yönünde şekillendirme işlevini engellemek isteyen bütün zorbaların eleştirildiği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r3.claim: It is unjust to stop someone who is rightly guided and urges others to reverence God and act responsibly from worship or religious duties.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r3.anchor: doğru yolda olan hem de başkalarına Allah’a saygılı olmayı ve sorumluluk şuuru içerisinde bulunmayı emreden bir kimsenin

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:12:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:12:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:12:anmerkung/r1.claim: The verb ittaqā and noun taqwā are discussed at 92:5 and connected here with istaġnā in verse 7.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:12:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zum Verb ittaqā und dem zugehörigen Substantiv taqwā s. die Anmerkung zu 92:5

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r3.claim: The would-be blocker should consider whether the worshipper is rightly guided and calls others to virtue; ignoring that possibility invites God’s wrath and is a satanic act.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r3.anchor: Is not there a chance that this servant of God be on the right path

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.claim: The first raʾayta takes the relative clause as its first object; in the second and third clauses the first object is omitted as a pronoun or demonstrative referring back to the forbidding man.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه أو اسم إشارة يشار به إليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.claim: Abu Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet while praying, but recoiled from a trench of fire, terror, and wings; the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb. The report is uncertain about whether the revelation was in Abu Hurayra's narration or another source.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r2.claim: The command to piety means sincerity and monotheism.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r2.anchor: أو أمر بالتقوى} يعني بالإخلاص والتوحيد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r4.claim: The rhetorical structure contrasts a guided servant who commands piety with a denier who turns away, exposing the strangeness of the persecutor's conduct.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r4.anchor: وتقدير نظم الآية: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى [والمنهي] (3) على الهدى، آمر بالتقوى، والناهي مكذب متول عن الإيمان

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.claim: The repeated أَرَأَيْتَ construction has the same grammatical function; its conditional is the second object, and its answer is omitted but supplied by the later condition. God sees the person's guidance and error.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.anchor: أرأيت تكرير للأول وكذا الذي في قوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.claim: One reading asks whether the forbidding person is himself guided and commands piety as he understands idol worship, or whether he is a denier who turns from truth; God sees all his states.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.anchor: إن كان ذلك الناهي على هدى فيما ينهى عنه، أو آمرا { بالتقوى }

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r5.claim: Another interpretation marvels that the worshipper is guided and commands piety while the forbidding person denies and turns away.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r5.anchor: وقيل المعنى { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا } يصلي والمنهي على الهدى

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r6.claim: A further reading shifts the second question to the unbeliever, as if a judge addresses each of two litigants in turn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r6.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في الثانية مع الكافر فإنه سبحانه وتعالى كالحاكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r7.claim: Mention of commanding piety heightens the rebuke; it is omitted from the description of the prohibition because forbidding prayer suffices, or because prayer represents action and invitation comprehensively.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r7.anchor: ولعله ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في التعجب والتوبيخ ولم يتعرض له في النهي

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.claim: Continuing al-Razi’s first solution, the rest of the surah came later about Abu Jahl, and the Prophet was directed to place these verses at its beginning.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.anchor: نزلت البقية في أبي جهل بن هشام، وأمر الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بضمها إلى أول السورة

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.claim: Al-Razi’s second solution reads الإنسان generically: despite creation and blessings, people transgress, forget their return, and forbid worship when they should follow guidance and enjoin piety.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.anchor: أن تحمل الآيات على عموم لفظها في الظاهر، وهو أن الإنسان، جملة الإنسان، خلقه الله من علق

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.claim: Both explanations are possible; the sequence suggests the passage followed public preaching and prayer, while a specific occasion does not prevent the wording from applying generally.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.anchor: وكلا الوجهين جائز. فسياق الآيات في السورة، يشعر بأنها نزلت بعد أن أبلغ المصطفى رسالة ربه

BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.claim: She argues that Quranic interrogative arayta usually omits its second object and directs attention instead to the lesson or warning; she cites several Meccan examples.
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.anchor: وإنما يستغنى عن هذا المفعول، بتقرير يلفت إلى موضع العبرة والنذير

BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.claim: The repeated arayta in this passage is a stylistic prompt to see and reflect on the warning; it need not take an explicit or inferred second object.
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.anchor: فلفتت إلى ما هو جدير بالرؤية والبصر والتدبر، وأغنت عما تعلق به النجاة من مفعول ثان

BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.claim: She urges readers to notice Quranic stylistic patterns even when they depart from school grammar and rhetoric, rather than forcing them into technical rules by conjecture.
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.anchor: فيشغلنا عن البيان العالى، تسوية الصنعة النحوية أو البلاغية، بالتأويل فيه والتقدير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p484/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p484/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p484/r3.claim: Enjoining piety builds the inner self with light through guidance and then orders outward conduct; the forbiddener would be urging the worshipper to keep serving his Lord and thereby avoid divine anger.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p484/r3.anchor: أي التي هي عماد الدين , وهي عمارة الباطن بالنور الناشئة عن الهدى

DURR:96:6/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:6/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:6/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:16/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.claim: He says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad; the guided one is Muhammad, the denier is Abu Jahl, his assembly is his clan, and ‘zabaniya’ means police in Arabic.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} قال: نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

TAB:96:12/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:12/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:12/r1.claim: The question asks whether Muhammad is on guidance, meaning upright and correct in prayer to his Lord, or whether he commands Abu Jahl to fear God and His punishment.
TAB:96:12/r1.anchor: أرأيت إن كان محمد على الهدى ،   يعني :  على استقامة وسداد في صلاته لربه

TAB:96:12/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:12/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:12/r2.claim: Qatada says Muhammad was on guidance and commanded piety.
TAB:96:12/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  { أرأيت إن كان على الهدى أو أمر بالتقوى } قال :  محمد كان على الهدى

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r6.claim: Another view addresses the unbeliever: would he forbid the worshipper if the prayer were guidance, calling to God, and commanding piety?
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r6.anchor: وقيل : { أرأيت } خطاب للكافر التفت إلى الكافر فقال : أرأيت يا كافر ، إن كانت صلاته هدى ودعاء إلى الله وأمراً بالتقوى

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī frames the challenge ironically: the forbider may regard idol worship as piety, yet from the Muslim view he denies truth and turns away from right religion.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري : ومعناه أخبرني عن من ينهى بعض عباد الله عن صلاته إن كان ذلك الناهي على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه من عبادة الله

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r11.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the servant as guided and enjoining piety, and the forbider as denying and turning away; Abū Jahl is rebuked for ignoring God’s sight. Prayer reforms the Prophet himself and enjoining piety reforms others, both of which troubled Abū Jahl.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r11.anchor: قال الفراء : المعنى { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } ، وهو على الهدى وأمر بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول عن الذكر

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats “did he not know?” as the omitted conditional answer, supplied by the second condition; he argues it may answer without fāʾ, by analogy with two interrogative examples.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r14.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : ما متعلق { أرأيت } ؟ قلت : { الذي ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r16.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī’s object analysis: the first object is the relative clause, while the second must be an interrogative clause, as in Qurʾānic parallels.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r16.anchor: وعندنا أن المفعول الثاني لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية ، كقوله : { أفرأيت الذي تولى وأعطى قليلاً وأكدى أعنده علم الغيب }

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r17.claim: Abū Ḥayyān analyzes the following “Have you seen?” forms as requiring omitted objects; their pronouns may refer to the forbider or, in the second instance, the servant, according to the disputed antecedent.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r17.anchor: ويجعل مفعول { أرأيت } الأولى هو الموصول ، وجاء بعده { أرأيت } ، وهي تطلب مفعولين ، وأرأيت الثانية كذلك

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r18.claim: The three governing verbs do not form a case of syntactic competition, because clauses cannot be pronominalized; the omissions are analyzed separately.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r18.anchor: وهؤلاء الطوالب ليس طلبها على طريق التنازع ، لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها ، وإنما ذلك من باب الحذف في غير التنازع

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r19.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects an interrogative clause answering a conditional without fāʾ: grammarians require it after constructions that entail a request, except in poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r19.anchor: وأما تجويز الزمخشري وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء ، فلا أعلم أحداً أجازه ، بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء

ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r14.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : ما متعلق { أرأيت } ؟ قلت : { الذي ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية

ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r16.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī’s object analysis: the first object is the relative clause, while the second must be an interrogative clause, as in Qurʾānic parallels.
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r16.anchor: وعندنا أن المفعول الثاني لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية ، كقوله : { أفرأيت الذي تولى وأعطى قليلاً وأكدى أعنده علم الغيب }

ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r17.claim: Abū Ḥayyān analyzes the following “Have you seen?” forms as requiring omitted objects; their pronouns may refer to the forbider or, in the second instance, the servant, according to the disputed antecedent.
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r17.anchor: ويجعل مفعول { أرأيت } الأولى هو الموصول ، وجاء بعده { أرأيت } ، وهي تطلب مفعولين ، وأرأيت الثانية كذلك

ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r18.claim: The three governing verbs do not form a case of syntactic competition, because clauses cannot be pronominalized; the omissions are analyzed separately.
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r18.anchor: وهؤلاء الطوالب ليس طلبها على طريق التنازع ، لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها ، وإنما ذلك من باب الحذف في غير التنازع

ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r19.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects an interrogative clause answering a conditional without fāʾ: grammarians require it after constructions that entail a request, except in poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN:96:13/r19.anchor: وأما تجويز الزمخشري وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء ، فلا أعلم أحداً أجازه ، بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء

ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r6.claim: Another view addresses the unbeliever: would he forbid the worshipper if the prayer were guidance, calling to God, and commanding piety?
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r6.anchor: وقيل : { أرأيت } خطاب للكافر التفت إلى الكافر فقال : أرأيت يا كافر ، إن كانت صلاته هدى ودعاء إلى الله وأمراً بالتقوى

ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī frames the challenge ironically: the forbider may regard idol worship as piety, yet from the Muslim view he denies truth and turns away from right religion.
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري : ومعناه أخبرني عن من ينهى بعض عباد الله عن صلاته إن كان ذلك الناهي على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه من عبادة الله

ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r11.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the servant as guided and enjoining piety, and the forbider as denying and turning away; Abū Jahl is rebuked for ignoring God’s sight. Prayer reforms the Prophet himself and enjoining piety reforms others, both of which troubled Abū Jahl.
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r11.anchor: قال الفراء : المعنى { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } ، وهو على الهدى وأمر بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول عن الذكر

ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats “did he not know?” as the omitted conditional answer, supplied by the second condition; he argues it may answer without fāʾ, by analogy with two interrogative examples.
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r14.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : ما متعلق { أرأيت } ؟ قلت : { الذي ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية

ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r16.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī’s object analysis: the first object is the relative clause, while the second must be an interrogative clause, as in Qurʾānic parallels.
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r16.anchor: وعندنا أن المفعول الثاني لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية ، كقوله : { أفرأيت الذي تولى وأعطى قليلاً وأكدى أعنده علم الغيب }

ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r17.claim: Abū Ḥayyān analyzes the following “Have you seen?” forms as requiring omitted objects; their pronouns may refer to the forbider or, in the second instance, the servant, according to the disputed antecedent.
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r17.anchor: ويجعل مفعول { أرأيت } الأولى هو الموصول ، وجاء بعده { أرأيت } ، وهي تطلب مفعولين ، وأرأيت الثانية كذلك

ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r18.claim: The three governing verbs do not form a case of syntactic competition, because clauses cannot be pronominalized; the omissions are analyzed separately.
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r18.anchor: وهؤلاء الطوالب ليس طلبها على طريق التنازع ، لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها ، وإنما ذلك من باب الحذف في غير التنازع

ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r19.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects an interrogative clause answering a conditional without fāʾ: grammarians require it after constructions that entail a request, except in poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN:96:14/r19.anchor: وأما تجويز الزمخشري وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء ، فلا أعلم أحداً أجازه ، بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء

ALUSI:96:10/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r33.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r33.claim: Next it warns him even on the supposition that he claims guidance in forbidding prayer or claims to command piety.
ALUSI:96:10/r33.anchor: وشنع سبحانه عليه ثانياً بنهيه عن ذلك وأوعده عليه أيضاً على تقدير أنه على زعمه على هدى ورشد

ALUSI:96:10/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r36.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:10/r36.claim: The majority read the first condition as a supposedly righteous course in forbidding worship of God or commanding piety while calling to idols, and the next as the prohibiter’s actual denial and turning away.
ALUSI:96:10/r36.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا حيث قالوا إن كان على طريقة سديدة

ALUSI:96:10/r48.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r48.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:10/r48.claim: Al-Farrāʾ’s reading makes the worshipper the subject of the second condition and the prohibiter the subject of the third: the worshipper is guided and commands piety, while the prohibiter denies and turns away—how astonishing.
ALUSI:96:10/r48.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً يصلي والمنهي على الهدى وأمر بالتقوى

ALUSI:96:10/r51.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r51.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r51.claim: In the split-address reading, “Would you forbid him?” may be the object of the question or the answer to its condition.
ALUSI:96:10/r51.anchor: وقوله أتنهاه يحتمل أنه جعله مفعولاً لرأيت ويحتمل أنه جواب الشرط

ALUSI:96:10/r52.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r52.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r52.claim: The mention of commanding piety in the second clause may cover the prohibiter’s verbal call, while prayer itself is an enacted call and therefore stronger; it was omitted from the first clause by anticipation.
ALUSI:96:10/r52.anchor: ولعل ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في الجملة الثانية لأن النهي على ما قيل كان عن الصلاة والأمر بها

ALUSI:96:10/r53.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r53.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:96:10/r53.claim: The Imām allows the whole address to be to the Prophet: if the sensible, wealthy man had chosen guidance and piety, would that not have been better than disbelief and obstructing worship?
ALUSI:96:10/r53.anchor: وجوز الإمام كون الخطاب في الكل له عليه الصلاة والسلام وقال في بيان معنى

ALUSI:96:10/r54.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r54.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:10/r54.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9–10 as exposing tyranny when a person feels self-sufficient, 96:11–12 as rebuking lost guidance and piety, and 96:13–14 as rebuking earned punishment and distance from God.
ALUSI:96:10/r54.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:10/r55.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r55.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r55.claim: Al-Ālūsī distances himself from ʿIṣām al-Dīn’s elaboration, inviting reflection and leaving the matter to God’s intended meaning.
ALUSI:96:10/r55.anchor: وهو كما ترى فتأمل جميع ما تقدم والله تعالى بمراده أعلم

ALUSI:96:12/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r24.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:12/r24.claim: The majority read the conditions as ironic concessions: the forbidder is supposedly guided or enjoining piety while calling to idols, yet in truth denies the truth and turns away; both conditions return to one point.
ALUSI:96:12/r24.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا حيث قالوا إن كان على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه من عبادة الله تعالى

ALUSI:96:12/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r34.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:12/r34.claim: Al-Farrāʾ assigns كان and أمر to the praying servant, but كذب and تولى and يعلم to the forbidder: the servant is guided and enjoins piety while the forbidder denies and turns away.
ALUSI:96:12/r34.anchor: وقيل الضميران في أن كان وأمر للعبد المصلي والضمائر في كذب وتولى ويعلم للذي ينهى وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء

ALUSI:96:12/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r35.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r35.claim: One view alternates addresses, asking the unbeliever whether he would forbid prayer that guides and calls to piety, then asking the Prophet whether the denier knows God sees him.
ALUSI:96:12/r35.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في أرأيت الثانية للكافر وفي الثانية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو عز وجل كالحاكم الذي حضر الخصمان

ALUSI:96:12/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r36.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r36.claim: Piety appears in the second question because the forbidder may have blocked both prayer and its call to piety; prayer alone is mentioned first to avoid repetition, and practical example is stronger than verbal exhortation.
ALUSI:96:12/r36.anchor: ولعل ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في الجملة الثانية لأن النهي على ما قيل كان عن الصلاة والأمر بها

ALUSI:96:12/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r37.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r37.claim: Another explanation says the first prohibition occurred during prayer but could concern prayer or something else; prayer perfects the worshipper and guides others, so forbidding during it could block both, hence the later mention of piety.
ALUSI:96:12/r37.anchor: وقيل المذكور أولاً ليس النهي عن الصلاة بل النهي حين الصلاة وهو محتمل أن يكون لها أو لغيرها

ALUSI:96:12/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r38.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:96:12/r38.claim: The Imam reads the second condition as asking whether it would not be better for the rational, wealthy man to pursue guidance and piety than to disbelieve and obstruct God’s worship; this reproaches him for losing higher ranks.
ALUSI:96:12/r38.anchor: وجوز الإمام كون الخطاب في الكل له عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI:96:12/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r39.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:12/r39.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as exposing tyranny born of self-sufficiency, 96:11 as reproaching lost guidance and piety, 96:13 as reproaching earned punishment and distance from God, and 96:14 as the threat after both reproaches.
ALUSI:96:12/r39.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:13/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r26.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:13/r26.claim: The majority do not limit the conditionals as al-Ālūsī did: the first supposes guidance or enjoining piety as claimed, the second denial and turning away as the commentators affirm.
ALUSI:96:13/r26.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا

ALUSI:96:13/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r36.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:13/r36.claim: Al-Farrāʾ assigns “was” and “commanded” to the praying servant, but “denied,” “turned away,” and “knows” to the prohibitor; the implied conclusion is how astonishing the case is.
ALUSI:96:13/r36.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً يصلي والمنهي على الهدى

ALUSI:96:13/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r38.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r38.claim: The second conditional mentions enjoining piety because the prohibition concerned prayer and its opposite; the phrase may have been omitted from the first conditional for brevity and supplied here.
ALUSI:96:13/r38.anchor: ولعل ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في الجملة الثانية لأن النهي على ما قيل كان عن الصلاة والأمر بها

ALUSI:96:13/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r39.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r39.claim: Prayer is named before verbal enjoining because it is an active call, stronger than speech; an exemplar’s action effectively says, “Do this.”
ALUSI:96:13/r39.anchor: واقتصر على ذكر الصلاة ولم يعكس لأن الأمر بالتقوى دعوة قولية والصلاة دعوة فعلية والفعل أقوى من القول

ALUSI:96:13/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r40.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r40.claim: A different view says the first clause describes forbidding someone during prayer, not necessarily forbidding prayer itself; since prayer both perfects the worshipper and calls others, the prohibition may target both.
ALUSI:96:13/r40.anchor: وعامة أحوال الصلاة لما انحصرت في تكميل أنفس المصلي بالعبادة وتكميل غيره بالدعوة

ALUSI:96:13/r41.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r41.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:96:13/r41.claim: The Imam reads the condition as asking whether a sensible, wealthy man would not do better to seek guidance and command piety than disbelieve and prohibit worship; God laments his forfeiture of high ranks for low ones.
ALUSI:96:13/r41.anchor: وجوز الإمام كون الخطاب في الكل له عليه الصلاة والسلام وقال في بيان معنى

ALUSI:96:13/r44.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r44.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:13/r44.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn takes the second question as rebuking lost benefit: what victory the man would have gained had he followed guidance or enjoined piety.
ALUSI:96:13/r44.anchor: عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

BAGHAWI:96:12/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:12/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:12/r1.claim: The command to piety means calling to sincerity and the oneness of God.
BAGHAWI:96:12/r1.anchor: أو أمر بالتقوى } يعني بالإخلاص والتوحيد

BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.claim: The sentence contrasts the forbidden servant, who is guided and commands piety, with the forbidding man, who denies and turns away; Baghawi calls the contrast astonishing.
BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.anchor: وتقدير نظم الآية : أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى ، والمنهي على الهدى ، آمر بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول عن الإيمان

BAYDAWI:96:12/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:12/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:12/r1.claim: The second “Have you considered?” repeats the first occurrence.
BAYDAWI:96:12/r1.anchor: { أرأيت إن كان على الهدى * أو أمر بالتقوى } أرأيت تكرير للأول

BAYDAWI:96:13/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:13/r5.claim: Piety is mentioned in the rebuke but not the prohibition because the prohibition concerned prayer and the command to piety; prayer alone suffices as an active call.
BAYDAWI:96:13/r5.anchor: ولعله ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في التعجب والتوبيخ ، ولم يتعرض له في النهي ؛ لأن النهي كان عن الصلاة والأمر بالتقوى

BAYDAWI:96:13/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:13/r6.claim: Alternatively, forbidding a praying servant may concern prayer or other matters; people’s states are encompassed by perfecting oneself through worship and others through calling them.
BAYDAWI:96:13/r6.anchor: أو لأن نهي العبد إذا صلى يحتمل أن يكون لها ولغيرها وعامة أحوالها محصورة في تكميل نفسه بالعبادة وغيره بالدعوة

BAYDAWI:96:14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:14/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:14/r5.claim: Piety is mentioned in the rebuke but not the prohibition because the prohibition concerned prayer and the command to piety; prayer alone suffices as an active call.
BAYDAWI:96:14/r5.anchor: ولعله ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في التعجب والتوبيخ ، ولم يتعرض له في النهي ؛ لأن النهي كان

BAYDAWI:96:14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:14/r6.claim: Alternatively, forbidding a praying servant may concern prayer or other matters; people’s states are encompassed by perfecting oneself through worship and others through calling them.
BAYDAWI:96:14/r6.anchor: أو لأن نهي العبد إذا صلى يحتمل أن يكون لها ولغيرها وعامة أحوالها محصورة في تكميل نفسه بالعبادة وغيره بالدعوة

BIQAI:96:12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:12/r1.claim: The alternative moves from a person's self-cultivation through guidance to his helping others: enjoining taqwa, the religion's pillar, illuminates the inward self and then the outward life.
BIQAI:96:12/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر ما لعله يكون عليه في تكميل نفسه

BIQAI:96:12/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:12/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:12/r2.claim: Taqwa is an inward illumination from guidance whose outward effects protect the worshipper from divine displeasure and destruction through devotion to the sovereign Lord.
BIQAI:96:12/r2.anchor: هي عمارة الباطن بالنور الناشئة عن الهدى

BIQAI:96:12/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:12/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:12/r3.claim: The response is omitted and supplied as Would this not be better for him? The verse urges people to test each action by evidence before proceeding, to know whether it is guidance and taqwa.
BIQAI:96:12/r3.anchor: والجواب محذوف تقديره : ألم يكن خيراً له

IBNATIYYA:96:12/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:12/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:12/r1.claim: Arayta is an interrogative challenge and, unlike knowledge-based vision, does not take two objects.
IBNATIYYA:96:12/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { أرأيت } توقيف ، وهو فعل لا يتعدى إلى مفعولين على حد الرؤية

IBNKATHIR:96:9/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:9/r3.claim: The man being restrained may be rightly guided in conduct or command piety in speech, while Abū Jahl threatens him for praying.

MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl tried to stop Muhammad praying and boasted of his council; al-ʿAlaq 96:10–13 was revealed, and Ibn Abbas says angels would seize him if he summoned them.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " جاء أبو جهل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI:96:11/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:11/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:11/r2.claim: The other reading refers to the Prophet: he was guided himself and commanded piety in obedience to his Lord.
MAWARDI:96:11/r2.anchor: الثاني : هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، كان على الهدى في نفسه ، وأمر بالتقوى في طاعة ربه .

MAWARDI:96:11/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:11/r3.claim: The address in araʾayta may be to the Prophet alone or generally to him and his community; either way, the passage asks about his guidance.
MAWARDI:96:11/r3.anchor: وفي قوله " أرأيْتَ " احتمال لوجهين : أحدهما : أنه خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم . الثاني : خطاب عام له ولأمته

MAWARDI:96:11/r4.speaker: author

NASAFI:96:12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:12/r1.claim: It asks whether he commands virtue and piety in what he himself considers worship of idols.
NASAFI:96:12/r1.anchor: أو كان آمراً بالمعروف والتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقد

QURTUBI:96:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:11/r1.claim: Addressing Abu Jahl, the verse asks whether, if Muhammad is guided and commands piety, the man forbidding his piety and prayer is not doomed.
QURTUBI:96:11/r1.anchor: أي أرأيت يا أبا جهل إن كان محمد على هذه الصفة ، أليس ناهيه عن التقوى

QURTUBI:96:12/r1.speaker: author

RAZI:96:12/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:12/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:12/r1.claim: One reading addresses the Prophet: the first and third clauses share this addressee, preserving the passage's rhetorical sequence.

RAZI:96:12/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:12/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:12/r2.claim: On this reading, the wording imagines the disbeliever becoming guided and reforming himself; this would suit a rational, prosperous man better than disbelief and hindering worship.

RAZI:96:12/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:12/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:96:12/r3.claim: A second reading addresses the disbeliever: God turns between parties as a judge might, asking whether he would still forbid Muhammad if his prayer guides and his call commands piety.
RAZI:96:12/r3.anchor: فلما قال للنبي : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى } التفت بعد ذلك إلى الكافر ، فقال : أرأيت يا كافر

RAZI:96:12/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:12/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:96:12/r4.claim: Prayer and calling people to God are both mentioned because these two aspects of the Prophet's conduct most troubled Abu Jahl.
RAZI:96:12/r4.anchor: الذي شق على أبي جهل من أفعال الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام هو هذان الأمران الصلاة والدعاء إلى الله

RAZI:96:12/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:12/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:96:12/r5.claim: The Prophet alternated between reforming himself through prayer and reforming others by commanding piety.
RAZI:96:12/r5.anchor: كان لا يوجد إلا في أحد أمرين

RAZI:96:12/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:12/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:96:12/r6.claim: The Prophet's prayer itself summoned people to faith: seeing him pray softened hearts, making action a stronger invitation than speech.
RAZI:96:12/r6.anchor: كان في صلاته على الهدى وآمرا بالتقوى
